posts.headline: One Nut Barner has now been silent through SIX straight editions, and Put it in Ra's absurd 20-8 record with a 1.5 average finish and zero rings remains the most disrespected résumé in Busters Anonymous history.
posts.detail: Two seasons, 20 wins, a best finish of 1st and worst of 2nd — yet somehow this is the quietest contender in the league. Rings mean nothing if you can't even show up to talk about the résumé.

posts.headline: Sasinci's World can't hide behind the draft anymore — Big Head still has to explain how a title banner hangs over a losing 13-15 career record.
posts.detail: One ring, a 5.5 average finish, and a manager who reportedly threatens to quit the league about once a month — Milk Man's pedigree is a magic trick that this column isn't falling for.

posts.headline: talentedtenthh enters year two with the single worst résumé in the league and nothing yet to suggest the untalented tenth learned a thing.
posts.detail: A 4-10 record and a dead-last 12th-place finish in his lone season is about as bottom-feeder as it gets — the name was always ironic, but so far the football matches it.

posts.headline: SwooshAnoosh owns the worst win percentage in the entire league and the preseason hype train has zero passengers.
posts.detail: A 5-9 rookie campaign and an 11th-place finish means the Prince of Persia is ruling over a kingdom of dust — nobody in the Titty Committee fears this throne.

posts.headline: BIBLE OR THE BELT drags a 13-14-1 career record and a defensive-player-first-overall sin into another draft season, and this league still hasn't forgiven it.
posts.detail: The Ultimate Light Skin loves asking folks whether they want the Bible or the Belt, but a 5.5 average finish says the real question is whether Eli can draft a skill player before it's too late.
